facts.title: Tigranes the Great
facts.text: Under his rule, Greater Armenia became the preeminent power east of the Roman world.

facts.title: Hostage of the Parthians
facts.text: He regained his freedom in 95 BC in exchange for ceding “seventy valleys” in Atropatene.

facts.title: “King of Kings”
facts.text: He pushed as far as Ecbatana, summer residence of the Parthian kings, and took the title arkayits arka.

facts.title: “From sea to sea”
facts.text: In 83 BC, Syria offered him its crown. His empire stretched from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean.

facts.title: Tigranakert
facts.text: A theater, ramparts, palaces: a Greek-inspired city whose king welcomed rhetoricians and philosophers.

facts.title: Peace with Pompey
facts.text: He renounced his external conquests and kept Greater Armenia, with the title of ally of Rome.

facts.title: An opera hero
facts.text: His epic runs from the pen of Movses Khorenatsi to the baroque operas of Vivaldi or Gluck.

ytTitle: Tigranes the Great and Armenia “from sea to sea”
ytLead: King from 95 to 55 BC, Tigranes the Great brought Armenia to its zenith: an empire from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean, a Greek-inspired capital at Tigranakert, and a peace negotiated with Rome.
